metadata.title: Mean and Median with statistics
metadata.description: Compute mean and median from a seeded list with the statistics module.

instructions.main: Given `data = [2, 4, 5, 6, 9]`, store the mean in `mean` and the median in `median` using Python's `statistics` module.
steps: Compute the mean with `mean = statistics.mean(data)` — for this list it is a decimal (5.2), not a whole number.

hints.message: Start with `import statistics`, then `mean = statistics.mean(data)` and `median = statistics.median(data)`.
`//` floors to a whole number, so the mean becomes 5 instead of 5.2. Use `statistics.mean(data)` (or `sum(data) / len(data)`) to keep the decimal.

evaluation.feedback_on_all_pass: You computed the mean (5.2) and median with the statistics module.

test_cases.feedback_on_pass: mean holds 5.2, the exact average of the list.
test_cases.feedback_on_fail: The mean of [2, 4, 5, 6, 9] is 5.2 — a fractional value. Check you did not floor it with `//` or replace it with the median.
Use the statistics module — `import statistics`, or bring the functions in with `from statistics import mean`.
